text.title: PM Certification Alignment 2026 Core Rules
text.summary: 14 testable rules grounding PM Certification Alignment 2026. Each pairs a binary check and a sourced rationale. 2026 PMP ECO domain weight deltas versus PMBOK 7, five exam themes, the anchor-citation requirement, and study-allocation rule. Priority areas for the +18% Business Environment shift, alignment-matrix management rules, and agent failure modes in certification content generation.

section.title: Background
section.p: Domain weights (PMBOK 7 → PMBOK 8): People 42% → 33% (-9%). Process 50% → 41% (-9%). Business Environment 8% → 26% (+18%). The +18% Business Environment shift is the most significant change in the PMP exam in a decade.

Five exam themes. Value Delivery: outcomes over outputs, benefits realization, value stream thinking. Governance: oversight, decision frameworks, stage gates. Sustainability: environmental, social, economic impact (ISO 14001, GRI, IFRS S1+S2). Stakeholder Engagement: communications integrated with stakeholder analysis. Practical Decision-Making: tailoring, situational trade-offs, hybrid approach selection.

rule.statement: Each methodology MUST be tagged with primary ECO 2026 domain ∈ {People, Process, Business Environment} and theme.
rule.rationale: Untagged methodologies cannot inform candidate study plans; explicit tagging makes coverage measurable.

rule.statement: Coverage analysis MUST compare methodology count per domain against ECO weight percentages (People 33%, Process 41%, Business Environment 26%).
rule.rationale: Coverage gaps correlate with exam-section underperformance; weight-vs-count comparison surfaces them.

rule.statement: Theme tags MUST come from the five canonical 2026 exam themes; ad-hoc themes forbidden.
rule.rationale: Ad-hoc themes fragment the rubric; five-theme constraint preserves comparability across cohorts.

rule.statement: Each coverage gap MUST trigger an action item with owner + due date (e.g. author missing methodology by Q3-2026).
rule.rationale: Gaps without actions persist for years; the rule forces backlog placement.

rule.statement: Candidate study plan MUST cite the rubric output; ad-hoc study plans forbidden.
rule.rationale: Ad-hoc study plans rely on instructor intuition; evidence-based plans tune time per ECO weight.

rule.statement: Do not allocate study time proportional to domain weight. Allocate proportional to (weight x current gap): a candidate already strong in People should deprioritize it even though it is 33% of the exam.
rule.rationale: Weight-proportional allocation optimizes for the exam's average candidate, not for the individual candidate's actual weaknesses. The maximum study ROI comes from closing the highest-weight gaps first.

rule.statement: Every coverage claim against an exam theme must cite a verbatim anchor from the official ECO PDF or PMBOK section (e.g., "ECO p.12 / PMBOK 8 §3.4"). Reject any claim without an anchor.
rule.rationale: Agents confidently fabricate PMBOK section references; a verbatim anchor forces verification against an indexed source and prevents teaching content that does not exist in the official material.

rule.statement: Sustainability content in PMBOK 8 is thin; supplement with ISO 14001, GRI standards, and IFRS S1+S2 for substantive study material. Never use agent-generated ISO clause text without cross-referencing the actual standard.
rule.rationale: Agents fabricate plausible-sounding ISO clauses; the real standards are the only authoritative source and must be the cross-reference for any sustainability claim.

rule.statement: Practical decision-making and tailoring questions resist memorization. Require scenario-based practice; rote-answer training agents perform poorly on these questions.
rule.rationale: PMP tailoring questions require reasoning from situational context, not recall; agents trained on rote patterns produce generic answers ("use both predictive and agile") that fail on specific scenarios.

rule.statement: For the +18% Business Environment shift, prioritize these methodology areas first before re-doing People or Process content: benefits-realization, value-stream-management, change-control, pm-framework-focus-areas. Add sustainability framing (ISO 14001, GRI) to each.
rule.rationale: The Business Environment domain grew from 8% to 26%; existing methodology libraries built on PMBOK 6/7 are structurally deficient here. Filling this gap delivers the highest exam-score improvement per study hour.

rule.statement: Store the alignment matrix in git as CSV with columns: domain, task_id, enablers, themes, covered_by (methodology slugs), evidence_anchor. Empty covered_by = gap. Never claim coverage without an evidence_anchor.
rule.rationale: A git-tracked matrix creates a diff history as the ECO changes; treating it as the system-of-record (and generating the wiki from it, not the reverse) prevents drift between documentation and actual coverage.

rule.statement: Re-run the alignment mapping after each annual ECO refresh and after any PMBOK edition release. Wire coverage_gaps.py to CI; failures open an issue assigned to the curriculum owner.
rule.rationale: ECO changes are typically announced 6 months before effective date; a CI-triggered gap report provides automated early warning rather than a manual audit cycle.

rule.statement: If preconditions for PM Certification Alignment 2026 fail (see Skip-If list in AGENTS.md), the operator MUST skip this methodology and document the fallback reason instead of fabricating an output.
rule.rationale: Applying PM Certification Alignment 2026 outside its envelope produces false-precision artefacts. Explicit skip preserves epistemic discipline.
